summary: Game crashes when player model is rendered after the player is stung by a bee
description: The bug When getting stung by a bee, the game crashes as soon as the player model is rendered. To reproduce There are multiple ways to reproduce this issue: Inventory - Get stung by a bee - Open your inventory Third-person camera - Enable third-person camera - Get stung by a bee Crash report 19w39a : [ crash-2019-09-27_13.19.08-client.txt] Description: Rendering entity in world java.lang.IllegalStateException: Not filled all elements of the vertex at cxk.a(SourceFile:253) at dwx.a(SourceFile:56) at dyd.a(SourceFile:48) at dyd.a(SourceFile:14) at duw.a(SourceFile:138) at dym.a(SourceFile:64) at dym.a(SourceFile:41) at dtz.a(SourceFile:268) at dtz.a(SourceFile:253) at dgt.a(SourceFile:134) at dgt.a(SourceFile:106) at dfx.render(SourceFile:82) at dgm.render(SourceFile:42) at dgt.render(SourceFile:86) at dpo.a(SourceFile:603) at dat.d(SourceFile:931) at dat.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Singleplayer world with default settings.
3. Enable the third-person camera view.
4. Get stung by a bee.
5. Wait for the player model to be rendered.
6. Observe that the game crashes immediately after the player model is rendered.
Observed Behavior: The game experiences a crash when the player model is rendered immediately after the player is stung by a bee. This issue can be reproduced in two specific scenarios: first, by getting stung by a bee and then opening the inventory, and second, by enabling the third-person camera, getting stung by a bee, and observing the crash. The crash report generated during this event indicates an IllegalStateException, specifically noting that not all elements of the vertex are filled. The error traceback shows that the crash occurs during the rendering process of the entity in the world, with multiple calls leading to the rendering functions in the game's code. This bug affects the player's experience significantly, as it results in an abrupt termination of the game upon being stung, making it crucial for developers to address the rendering issue related to the player model.
Expected Behavior: When a player gets stung by a bee, the game should continue to function normally without crashing. The player model should render correctly, allowing the player to interact with their inventory or switch to third-person camera mode without any issues. The game should maintain stability, enabling the player to experience the effects of the bee sting, such as receiving damage or status effects, without encountering any rendering errors.
